name: writex_agent
description: Tool contract for external AI agents controlling WriteX through the running web app. Agents should discover tools, choose the right operation, then call a browser bridge. They should not hand-write .writexproj JSON unless explicitly exporting or importing.

runtime.postMessageBridge: window.postMessage({ type: 'writex-agent-call', id, name, args }, window.location.origin)
runtime.customEventBridge: window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('writex-agent-call', { detail: { id, name, args } }))

priority: Read this manifest from the link[rel="agent-tools"] href or from /scribyx/writex-agent-tool.json.
Open the app page and inspect #writex-agent-manifest if available.
If direct page globals are visible, use window.writexAgent.listTools() and window.writexAgent.callTool(name, args).
If window.writexAgent is undefined, do not treat that as failure. Use the hash bridge and read #writex-agent-result from the DOM.
Do not automate the visible editor/contenteditable UI unless both direct and hash bridges fail.

nonDestructiveSmokeTest.name: getProject
nonDestructiveSmokeTest.expectedResultShape: outer result.ok true, inner result.result.ok true, inner result.result.data contains title and chapters

importantNotes: Some browser automation environments evaluate JavaScript in an isolated world where window.writexAgent is not visible even though the app installed it correctly.
Changing the URL hash is the compatibility path because the real page receives hashchange in its own main world.
The DOM result script is intentionally outside #root so React will not overwrite it.
A large getProject result can be big; use it for smoke tests and id resolution, then call narrower tools when available.

agentWorkflow: First choose a bridge using firstTimeAgentProtocol. For generic Playwright/DOM agents, prefer hashBridgeWithDomResult.
Call listTools() through the chosen bridge to inspect available operations and parameter schemas.
Call getProject before mutating so ids for chapters, categories, entities, maps, and snapshots are known.
Use createChapter, createEntity, linkText, createGraphSnapshot, addGraphNode, and addGraphEdge instead of constructing JSON manually.
Commit chapter snapshots after meaningful chapter changes.
Commit a global snapshot after a coherent project milestone.
Call exportProject only at the end when a .writexproj payload is needed.
Call createShareLink when the user wants a serverless URL that embeds the current story for another browser.

dispatcherExamples.call: await window.writexAgent.callTool('createChapter', { title: 'Capitolo 1', body: 'Anna entra nella serra.' })
await window.writexAgent.callTool('createEntity', { categoryId: 'cat-chars', name: 'Anna', avatar: 'An', desc: 'Curiosa e prudente.' })

dispatcherExamples.intent: Link exact text to an entity

dispatcherExamples.call: await window.writexAgent.callTool('commitGlobal', { label: 'Bozza completa' }); const project = await window.writexAgent.callTool('exportProject', {})

bridgeExamples.call: window.postMessage({ type: 'writex-agent-call', id: 'cmd-1', name: 'createChapter', args: { title: 'Capitolo 1', body: 'Anna entra nella serra.' } }, window.location.origin)
location.hash = 'writex-agent=' + encodeURIComponent(JSON.stringify({ id: 'cmd-2', name: 'commitGlobal', args: { label: 'Bozza completa' } }))

bridgeExamples.intent: Read URL command result from DOM

bridgeExamples.call: Open /scribyx/#writex-project=<encoded payload>. The app imports the embedded project into the recipient browser.

toolsSourceOfTruth: At runtime, call window.writexAgent.listTools(). The returned data includes each tool name, description, whenToUse guidance, and JSON Schema parameters.
